definition: The space mapping methodology for modeling and design optimization of engineering systems was first discovered by John Bandler in 1993.
details: It uses relevant existing knowledge to speed up model generation and design optimization of a system. The knowledge is updated with new validation information from the system when available.

explainer.lead: Space mapping is a methodology for modeling and design optimization of engineering systems, first discovered by John Bandler in 1993. It uses existing knowledge to speed up model generation and design optimization.

tiers.eli5: It is a shortcut for engineering design: start from an already-known simpler model and keep correcting it with real measurements.
tiers.practitioner: Use it to speed up optimization by leaning on an existing coarse model and updating that knowledge with new validation data from the system. Neglecting to refresh with real validation erodes its accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: A methodology for modeling and design optimization of engineering systems, discovered by John Bandler in 1993. It uses relevant existing knowledge to speed up model generation and optimization, updated with new validation information when available.

explainer.example: An engineer optimizes a cheap approximate model of a system, then uses measurements from the real system to update the mapping toward the true design.
